title: Pehea e hiki ai i laila?
description: Ten short stories about getting around the islands: the winding road to Hāna, a traffic jam with Hawaiian radio, a survey on the bus, an outrigger canoe in a storm, a walk through an ahupuaʻa, a lava flow that closes the roads, a yellow taxi in Waikīkī, driving food to a lūʻau, a runaway rabbit and a ferry to a golf course on Lānaʻi.

lessons.title: Nā hulina o ke alanui i Hāna
lessons.summary: Kēhaunani and her brother Keawalau drive the winding road from Kahului to Hāna: they go slowly through the dense forest, pick mountain apples, stop at a view, swim in a cold pool under a waterfall, climb a trail and drive home carefully in the dark.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Kēhaunani a me kona kaikunāne ʻo Keawalau ma Kahului, ma ka mokupuni ʻo Maui. I kekahi Pōʻaono, ua hoʻoholo lāua e holo i Hāna ma ke kaʻa. Wahi a ka poʻe, aia he ʻeono haneli hulina ma ke alanui i Hāna a kokoke i kanaono alahaka. "E akahele kāua," wahi a Kēhaunani. "Ke holo wikiwiki ke kaʻa ma kēia mau hulina, hiki ke loaʻa ka pōʻino."

Ua hoʻokele ʻo Keawalau i ke kaʻa. Ma hope o Pāʻia, ua hoʻomaka nā hulina. Ua hāliu ke alanui i ka ʻākau, a laila ua hāliu ia i ka hema, a ua hāliu hou ia i ka ʻākau. Ua paʻapū ka ululāʻau ma nā ʻaoʻao ʻelua o ke alanui. Ua paʻapū pū ke alanui i nā kaʻa o nā malihini. No laila, ua holo mālie a akahele ʻo Keawalau.

Ma kekahi hulina, ua ʻike ʻo Kēhaunani i nā kumu ʻōhiʻa ʻai. Ua ʻulaʻula nā hua ʻōhiʻa ma nā lālā. Ua kū lāua, a ua ʻohi lāua i kekahi mau hua ʻōhiʻa. ʻOno a momona nā hua. Ua minoʻaka ʻo Keawalau i kona ʻai ʻana.

Ma hope iho, ua hāliu ʻo Keawalau i ke kaʻa i kekahi wahi kū kaʻa ma ka pali. Mai laila, ua nānā lāua i kekahi ʻikena nani loa: ke kai uliuli ma lalo, nā pali ʻōmaʻomaʻo, a me kekahi wailele keʻokeʻo. "No kēia ʻikena kāua i hele mai ai," wahi a Kēhaunani me ka minoʻaka.

Ma hope o Hāna, ua hiki lāua i kekahi loko wai ma lalo o kekahi wailele. Ua lele ʻo Keawalau i loko o ka wai, a ua ʻau ʻo ia a hiki i ka wailele. "Huʻihuʻi!" wahi āna. "Huʻihuʻi loa kēia wai!" Ua ʻau pū ʻo Kēhaunani, a ua ʻakaʻaka lāua.

A laila, ua hele wāwae lāua ma kekahi alahele i uka. He piʻina lōʻihi ia ma waena o ka ululāʻau ʻohe. Ma waena o ka piʻina, ua luhi ʻo Keawalau, akā ua minoʻaka ʻo Kēhaunani. "Ke pau ka piʻina, e ʻike ana kāua i ka wailele nui," wahi āna. Ua pololei ʻo ia: ma ka hope o ka piʻina, aia kekahi wailele kiʻekiʻe loa.

I ke ahiahi, ua hoʻi lāua i Kahului. Ua ʻeleʻele ka lani, a ua holo akahele loa ʻo Keawalau ma nā hulina a pau.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia hulina ma ke alanui i Hāna?
Wahi a ka poʻe, aia he ʻeono haneli hulina, a kokoke i kanaono alahaka.
No ke aha i holo mālie ai ʻo Keawalau?
No ka mea ua paʻapū ke alanui i nā kaʻa o nā malihini.
He aha nā hua a lāua i ʻohi ai?
Ua ʻohi lāua i nā hua ʻōhiʻa.
Pehea ka wai ma lalo o ka wailele?
Huʻihuʻi loa ka wai.

lessons.title: Ka lekiō ma ke alanui paʻapū
lessons.summary: Kekūmano drives from Kapolei to his Honolulu office; stuck in traffic he sighs and complains about wasted time, until a Hawaiian radio programme with a native speaker from Niʻihau turns the drive into lesson time.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Kekūmano ma Kapolei, a hana ʻo ia ma kekahi keʻena ma ke kaona o Honolulu. I kēlā me kēia kakahiaka, hoʻokele ʻo ia i kona kaʻa i ka hana. I ka pō, ke kākaʻikahi nā kaʻa, he hapahā hola wale nō ka holo ʻana. I ke kakahiaka naʻe, paʻapū ke alanui i nā kaʻa, a hoʻokahi hola a me ka hapahā ka holo ʻana.

I kekahi kakahiaka, ua kū nā kaʻa a pau ma ke alanui. Ua ukiuki loa ʻo Kekūmano. Ua ʻū ʻo ia. "Ke māuna nei au i koʻu manawa," wahi āna. "Māuna au i ʻelua hola i kēlā me kēia lā!" Ua kē nā kānaka o Kapolei i ke aupuni no nā makahiki he nui, akā ʻaʻole i loli ke alanui.

Ua wehe ʻo Kekūmano i ka lekiō. Ua lohe ʻo ia i kekahi polokalamu ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi. "Welina mai, e nā hoaaloha ma ke alanui!" wahi a ka wahine o ka polokalamu. "I kēia kakahiaka, he malihini kūikawā ko kākou: he mānaleo mai Niʻihau mai." Ua ʻōlelo ka mānaleo no kona wā kamaliʻi. I kēlā wā, ʻaʻohe kaʻa ma Niʻihau. Ua hele ka poʻe ma ka lio a ma ka wāwae.

Ua noho mū ʻo Kekūmano, a ua hoʻolohe ʻo ia. Ua ʻōlelo ka mānaleo me ka leo mālie. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i ʻū hou. Ua hoʻohala ʻo ia i ka manawa me ka hoʻolohe ʻana i ka lekiō. Ua ʻai ʻo ia i kāna kanauika moa me ka noho mū.

Ua hiki ʻo ia i ke keʻena i ka hola 9. Ua nīnau mai kona hoa hana, "Ua ukiuki paha ʻoe?" "ʻAʻole," wahi āna me ka minoʻaka. "Ua aʻo au i nā huaʻōlelo hou mai kekahi mānaleo."

Mai ia lā mai, ua hoʻolohe ʻo Kekūmano i ka polokalamu i kēlā me kēia kakahiaka. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i māuna hou i kona manawa; ua hoʻohala ʻo ia i ka manawa me ke aʻo ʻana. Ua ʻai ʻo ia i kāna kanauika ma ke alanui. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i kē hou no ke alanui. A i kēlā me kēia kakahiaka, ʻōlelo ka wahine o ka lekiō, "Welina mai!" a pane ʻo Kekūmano i loko o kona kaʻa, "Welina!"

Nā nīnau:
Pehea ka lōʻihi o ka holo ʻana i ka pō?
He hapahā hola wale nō.
No ke aha i ukiuki ai ʻo Kekūmano?
No ka mea ua kū nā kaʻa a pau, a ua māuna ʻo ia i kona manawa.
He aha ka mea a ka mānaleo i ʻōlelo ai?
Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia no kona wā kamaliʻi ma Niʻihau.
Pehea ʻo Kekūmano i hoʻohala ai i ka manawa?
Ua noho mū ʻo ia a hoʻolohe i ka lekiō, a ua ʻai ʻo ia i kāna kanauika.

lessons.title: Ka anamanaʻo ma ke kaʻa ʻōhua
lessons.summary: Leimana, a student at Mānoa, rides the bus for a class survey on how people get around Honolulu; she helps an old man who forgot his glasses, and ninety riders answer her questions.
lessons.text:
ʻO Leimana ka inoa oʻu. He haumāna au ma ke kulanui ma Mānoa. I kēia kau, ua hāʻawi mai ko mākou kumu i kekahi hana: e hana i kekahi anamanaʻo no ka poʻe e holo ana ma ke kaʻa ʻōhua. Makemake ʻo ia e ʻike pehea ka poʻe e hele ai i ka hana.

Ua kākau au i ʻumi nīnau ma kekahi pepa. ʻO ka nīnau mua, ʻo ia ka makahiki o ke kanaka. ʻO ka nīnau ʻelua, ʻo ia ke keka: he kāne, he wahine, a i ʻole he ʻano ʻē aʻe. ʻO nā nīnau ʻē aʻe, no ko lākou holo ʻana ma ke kaʻa.

I ka Pōʻakahi, ua eʻe au i ke kaʻa ma Kalihi me hoʻokahi haneli pepa. Ua ʻī aku au i ka poʻe, "Aloha ʻoukou! He haumāna au. Ke hana nei au i kekahi anamanaʻo. Inā ʻae ʻoukou, e ʻoluʻolu, e pane mai i kēia mau nīnau." Ua hāʻawi au i kekahi pepa i kekahi wahine. "Nāu kēia pepa," wahi aʻu. "Aia nā nīnau āu e pane ai ma nā ʻaoʻao ʻelua o ka pepa."

Ua nānā mai kekahi kanaka kahiko. Ua ʻī mai ʻo ia, "ʻAʻole hiki iaʻu ke heluhelu. Ua poina iaʻu koʻu makaaniani ma ka hale." Ua heluhelu au i nā nīnau nona, a ua kākau au i kāna mau pane. "He kanahiku oʻu makahiki," i ʻī mai ai ʻo ia, "a ua holo au ma ke kaʻa ʻōhua i kēlā me kēia lā no nā makahiki he kanaono." Ua ʻī hou mai ʻo ia, "Mahalo iā ʻoe!"

Ua holo au ma ke kaʻa i nā lā a pau o kēlā pule. Ma ka Pōʻalima, ua pane mai he kanaiwa kānaka. Ma loko o nā kānaka he kanaiwa, he kanahiku i holo ma ke kaʻa ʻōhua i kēlā me kēia lā.

Ua hōʻike au i ka anamanaʻo i ka papa. Ua ʻī mai ke kumu, "Maikaʻi kāu hana. He aha ka mea āu i aʻo ai?" Ua pane au, "Holo ka poʻe he nui ma ke kaʻa ʻōhua no ka mea pipiʻi nā kaʻa." Ua ʻī mai ke kumu, "Nāu e hōʻike i kēia anamanaʻo i ka poʻe o ke kulanui i kēia mahina aʻe."

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a ke kumu i hāʻawi ai iā Leimana?
E hana i kekahi anamanaʻo no ka poʻe e holo ana ma ke kaʻa ʻōhua.
He aha ka nīnau ʻelua ma ka pepa?
ʻO ke keka ka nīnau ʻelua.
No ke aha i hiki ʻole ai i ke kanaka kahiko ke heluhelu?
Ua poina iā ia kona makaaniani ma ka hale.
ʻEhia kānaka i pane mai?
He kanaiwa kānaka i pane mai, a he kanahiku o lākou i holo i kēlā me kēia lā.

lessons.title: Ka waʻa ma ke kai ʻino
lessons.summary: Two friends from Kaunakakai paddle their small outrigger canoe out for ono; a storm rocks them, the sea pours in, the float is damaged on a rock, the canoe runs aground and they carry it home with the fish.
lessons.text:
He mau hoaaloha ʻo Kahalepuna lāua ʻo Kealiʻikaua. Noho lāua ma Kaunakakai, ma Molokaʻi. He waʻa liʻiliʻi ko lāua, me ka ama ma kekahi ʻaoʻao. Mālama ka ama i ka waʻa i luna o ke kai. Me ka ʻole o ka ama, huli koke ka waʻa.

I kekahi kakahiaka, ua hali lāua i ka waʻa mai ka hale a hiki i ke kahakai. Kaumaha ka waʻa, no laila ua hali mālie lāua. Ua hoe lāua i waho, i ke kai hohonu, no ka lawaiʻa ʻana i ka ono. He iʻa nui ka ono, a ʻono loa kona ʻiʻo. Makemake nui ka ʻohana o Kahalepuna i ka ono.

Ma hope o ʻelua hola, ua paʻa kekahi ono nui i ke kaula. Ua huki ʻo Kealiʻikaua, a ua kōkua ʻo Kahalepuna. Ua hoʻokomo lāua i ka ono i loko o ka waʻa. Ua hauʻoli loa lāua.

A laila, ua hoʻomaka ka ʻino. Ua ʻeleʻele ka lani, a ua pā mai ka makani ikaika. Ua hoʻoluli nā nalu i ka waʻa. Ua komo lāua i ko lāua mau ʻahu ua. Ua hanini mai ke kai ma luna o ka ʻaoʻao o ka waʻa, a ua piha ka waʻa i ka wai. Ua kulu ka wai mai ko lāua lauoho a me ko lāua mau ʻahu.

Ua hoe ikaika lāua i uka. Ua hoʻoluli hou ka nalu i ka waʻa, a ua kuʻi ka ama i kekahi pōhaku. Ua ʻinoʻino ka ama, a ua mahae ka ʻahu o Kahalepuna ma ka pōhaku. Ua hanini hou mai ke kai i loko o ka waʻa. Ma hope iho, ua ili ka waʻa ma ke one, ma kahi pāpaʻu kokoke i ke kahakai. ʻAʻole hiki iā lāua ke hoe hou, no laila ua lele lāua i ke kai a ua ʻau lāua me ka waʻa a hiki i ke kahakai.

Ma ke kahakai, ua hali lāua i ka waʻa i luna o ke one. Ua kulu ka wai mai ka ʻahu mahae o Kahalepuna. Ua nānā lāua i ka ama ʻinoʻino. "Hiki iā kāua ke hoʻoponopono i ka ama," wahi a Kealiʻikaua. "Ua mahae kou ʻahu, akā aia nō ka ono me kāua!" Ua ʻakaʻaka lāua. I kēlā ahiahi, ua ʻai ka ʻohana i ka ono.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a ka ama?
Mālama ka ama i ka waʻa i luna o ke kai.
He aha ka iʻa a lāua i hopu ai?
Ua hopu lāua i kekahi ono nui.
He aha ka mea i hanini mai ma luna o ka waʻa?
Ua hanini mai ke kai.
Ma hea i ili ai ka waʻa?
Ua ili ka waʻa ma ke one, kokoke i ke kahakai.

lessons.title: Mai uka a i kai
lessons.summary: A class from a Hawaiian-medium school walks through an ahupuaʻa at Heʻeia with Uncle Kaholokai, from the forest past the taro patches and gardens to an old temple and the shore, where he tells them about his family's shark guardian.
lessons.text:
I kekahi Pōʻalima, ua hele nā haumāna o ka papa ʻelima o kekahi kula kaiapuni i Heʻeia, ma Oʻahu. Ua hālāwai lākou me ʻAnakala Kaholokai. He mahiʻai kalo ʻo ʻAnakala Kaholokai, a ua aʻo ʻo ia i nā keiki no ka ahupuaʻa.

"He ʻāpana ʻāina ka ahupuaʻa," wahi a ka ʻanakala. "Hoʻomaka ka ahupuaʻa ma luna o ka mauna, a pau ia ma ke kai. Ma ka wā kahiko, ua loaʻa i ka poʻe o ka ahupuaʻa nā mea a pau: ka lāʻau a me nā manu ma uka, ke kalo ma waena, a me ka iʻa ma kai."

Ua hoʻomaka lākou ma uka, ma ka ululāʻau. Ua paʻapū ke alahele i nā aʻa o nā kumulāʻau. "E akahele i nā aʻa," wahi a ka ʻanakala. "Inā ʻaʻole ʻoukou e nānā i nā aʻa, e hina ana ʻoukou." Ma luna o kekahi kumu ʻōhiʻa, ua ʻike kekahi kaikamahine, ʻo Hiʻilani, i nā ʻōpuʻu. "ʻAʻole i mohala nā ʻōpuʻu," wahi a ka ʻanakala. "Ma kēia mahina aʻe, e lilo ana nā ʻōpuʻu i mau pua ʻulaʻula."

Ma waena o ke awāwa, ua hiki lākou i nā loʻi kalo. Ua kahe ka wai mai ke kahawai i loko o nā loʻi. Ua kū nā lau kalo ʻōmaʻomaʻo ma luna o ka wai. Ua komo nā keiki i loko o kekahi loʻi, a ua huki lākou i ka mauʻu mai waena o ke kalo. "Ke ulu ka mauʻu, ʻaʻole ulu maikaʻi ke kalo," wahi a ka ʻanakala. Ma ka ʻaoʻao o nā loʻi, aia nā kīhāpai maiʻa a me nā kīhāpai lāʻau lapaʻau.

Kokoke i ke kai, ua ʻike lākou i kekahi pā pōhaku kahiko. "He heiau kēia," wahi a ka ʻanakala. "Ma ka wā kahiko, ua kapu kēia wahi. ʻAʻole ia he wahi noa. Ma waho o ka heiau naʻe, ua noa ka ʻāina, a ua hiki i nā kānaka a pau ke hele ma laila."

Ma kahakai, ua ʻike ʻo Hiʻilani i kekahi manō ma ka wai pāpaʻu. Ua makaʻu ʻo ia, akā ua minoʻaka ka ʻanakala. "ʻO ka manō ka ʻaumakua o koʻu ʻohana," wahi āna. "Mālama mākou i ka manō, a mālama ko mākou ʻaumakua iā mākou."

Nā nīnau:
Ma hea e hoʻomaka ai ka ahupuaʻa?
Hoʻomaka ka ahupuaʻa ma luna o ka mauna.
He aha ka mea a nā keiki i huki ai mai ka loʻi?
Ua huki lākou i ka mauʻu mai waena o ke kalo.
He aha ka mea a Hiʻilani i ʻike ai ma luna o ke kumu ʻōhiʻa?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i nā ʻōpuʻu.
He aha ka ʻaumakua o ka ʻohana o ka ʻanakala?
ʻO ka manō ka ʻaumakua o kona ʻohana.

lessons.title: Ka pāhoehoe ma Puna
lessons.summary: A lava flow creeps toward Wehilani's village near Pāhoa: the county closes the roads, people gather at the school, she stores food and water, drives a new road over old lava, her son falls ill from the smoke, and at last the flow stops.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Wehilani a me kāna keiki kāne ʻo Kaʻiamaka ma kekahi kauhale liʻiliʻi kokoke i Pāhoa, ma Puna. I kekahi makahiki, ua kahe mai ka pele mai ka lua pele mai. He pāhoehoe ia. Kahe mālie ka pāhoehoe ma ka ʻāina e like me ka wai, a ma hope o kona maloʻo ʻana, he pōhaku ʻeleʻele ia.

I kēlā me kēia lā, ua neʻe ka pāhoehoe i mua. Ua uhi ʻia he kanaono ʻakele, a laila he haneli ʻakele. Ua hoʻākoakoa ke kalana i ka poʻe o ke kauhale ma ke kula. Ua hoʻākoakoa he mau haneli kānaka. Ua ʻōlelo kekahi luna, "E pani ana mākou i ke alanui. ʻAʻole hiki i kekahi ke hele i loko o kahi kahahānai o ʻelua mile mai ka pele."

Ma hope o ka hālāwai, ua hoʻāhu ʻo Wehilani i ka ʻai a me ka wai ma kona hale. Ua hoʻāhu ʻo ia i nā pahu wai, ka laiki, a me nā kini ʻai.

Ma hope o hoʻokahi pule, ua pani ʻia ke alanui nui. Ua neo ke alanui; ʻaʻohe kaʻa. ʻUʻuku wale nō nā kaʻa ma ke kauhale, a ʻuʻuku nā kānaka ma nā hale kūʻai. I ka hele ʻana i ka hana, ua holo ʻo Wehilani ma kekahi ala hou ma luna o ka pele kahiko. Nihoa nā pōhaku ʻeleʻele ma nā ʻaoʻao o ke ala. I kekahi lā, ua ʻoki kekahi pōhaku nihoa i ka huila o kona kaʻa.

Ua hoʻomaʻi ka uahi o ka pele i kekahi poʻe o ke kauhale. Ua hoʻomaʻi ka uahi iā Kaʻiamaka, a ua ʻeha kona ʻāʻī. No laila, ua noho ʻo ia i loko o ka hale me nā puka i pani ʻia.

I kekahi pō, ua kū ʻo Wehilani lāua ʻo Kaʻiamaka ma waho o ka hale. Ua ʻike leʻa lāua i ke ahi ʻulaʻula o ka pāhoehoe ma ka ululāʻau. Ua lohe leʻa lāua i ka ʻā ʻana o nā kumulāʻau. Ma hope o kekahi mau pule, ua kū ka pāhoehoe ma mua o kona hiki ʻana i ke kauhale. Ua wehe hou ʻia ke alanui, a ua hoʻi mai nā kaʻa. ʻAʻole i neo hou ke alanui.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ke ʻano o ka pele i kahe mai?
He pāhoehoe ia.
ʻEhia ʻakele i uhi ʻia e ka pele?
Ua uhi ʻia he haneli ʻakele.
Ma hea i hoʻākoakoa ai nā kānaka?
Ua hoʻākoakoa lākou ma ke kula.
He aha ke kahahānai i pani ʻia?
He kahahānai o ʻelua mile mai ka pele.
He aha ka mea a Wehilani i hoʻāhu ai?
Ua hoʻāhu ʻo ia i ka ʻai a me ka wai.

lessons.title: Ke kaʻa lenalena
lessons.summary: Kanehoa drives a yellow taxi in Waikīkī at night: a woman is captivated by the neon lights, her bearded husband falls asleep and cannot pay the fare, and the next day Kanehoa gropes under the back seat and finds her precious diamond ring.
lessons.text:
He mea hoʻokele kaʻa hoʻolimalima ʻo Kanehoa ma Waikīkī. Lenalena kona kaʻa, a ʻike koke ka poʻe i ke kaʻa lenalena ma ke alanui. Hana ʻo ia i ka pō, ke ʻālohilohi nā kukui nīane o nā hōkele a me nā hale ʻaina.

I kekahi pō, ua eʻe mai kekahi kāne a me kekahi wahine, he mau malihini mai Kaleponi mai. He ʻumiʻumi lōʻihi ko ke kāne, a he lei ko ka wahine. Ua punihei ka wahine i nā kukui nīane. "Nani loa nā kukui!" wahi āna. Ua nānā ʻo ia ma waho o ka pukaaniani i nā kukui nīane ʻulaʻula, uliuli, a ʻōmaʻomaʻo. Ua punihei loa ʻo ia, a ʻaʻole ʻo ia i walaʻau.

Ua luhi ke kāne ʻumiʻumi. Ma hope o ʻelima minuke, ua hiamoe ʻo ia ma ka noho hope. Ua hiamoe ʻo ia a hiki i ko lākou hōkele ma kekahi ʻaoʻao o Waikīkī. "He kanakolu kālā ke kāki," wahi a Kanehoa. Ua ala ke kāne ʻumiʻumi, a ua ʻimi ʻo ia i kāna kālā. ʻAʻohe ona kālā. "Ua waiho au i kaʻu kālā ma ka hale ʻaina!" wahi āna. "He ʻaiʻē kaʻu iā ʻoe. E uku ana au i ka ʻaiʻē i ka lā aʻe." Ua ʻae ʻo Kanehoa. Ua kākau ʻo ia i ka nui o ke kāki ma kekahi pepa.

I ka lā aʻe, ua kelepona mai ka wahine. "Ua nalowale koʻu komo lima kaimana," wahi āna. "He komo makamae loa ia. No koʻu kupuna wahine mai ia. Aia paha ia i loko o kou kaʻa."

Ua ʻimi ʻo Kanehoa i loko o kona kaʻa. Ua ʻeleʻele ka hale kaʻa, a ua hāhā ʻo ia ma lalo o ka noho hope me kona lima. Ua hāhā ʻo ia ma nā kihi a pau. A laila, ua pā kona lima i kekahi mea liʻiliʻi a paʻakikī: ʻo ke komo kaimana!

Ua hoʻi ʻo Kanehoa i ka hōkele. Ua hāʻawi ʻo ia i ke komo makamae i ka wahine, a ua minoʻaka ka wahine. "He makamae kēia kaimana iaʻu ma mua o nā mea a pau," wahi āna. Ua uku ke kāne ʻumiʻumi i kāna ʻaiʻē, a ua hāʻawi pū ʻo ia i kekahi kālā hou aʻe no ka mahalo.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka waihoʻoluʻu o ke kaʻa o Kanehoa?
Lenalena kona kaʻa.
He aha ka mea i punihei ai ka wahine?
Ua punihei ʻo ia i nā kukui nīane.
Ua aha ke kāne ʻumiʻumi ma ka noho hope?
Ua hiamoe ʻo ia.
He aha ke kāki?
He kanakolu kālā ke kāki.
Ma hea i loaʻa ai ke komo kaimana?
Ua loaʻa ke komo ma lalo o ka noho hope.

lessons.title: Ka lūʻau ma Kāneʻohe
lessons.summary: Lehuanani and her son Kaʻeloa prepare food in Waiʻanae for her grandchild's first-birthday lūʻau, gather kiawe wood, load the truck and drive it all over the mountains to Kāneʻohe, where the elders drink ʻawa from bamboo cups.
lessons.text:
I kekahi Pōʻaono, ua mālama ʻia kekahi lūʻau ma Kāneʻohe no ka lā hānau mua o ka moʻopuna a Lehuanani. ʻO Lehuanani a me kāna keiki kāne ʻo Kaʻeloa ka poʻe kuke. Noho lāua ma Waiʻanae, ma Oʻahu.

I ka Pōʻalima, ua hoʻomākaukau lāua i ka ʻai. Ua hoʻokala ʻo Kaʻeloa i nā pahi a pau. "ʻAʻole maikaʻi ka ʻoki ʻana me ka pahi i hoʻokala ʻole ʻia," wahi a kona makuahine. Ua ʻoki ʻo ia i ʻumi ʻakaʻakai no ka iʻa, a ua kahe ka wai mai kona mau maka. Ua kaka ʻo Lehuanani i nā lau kalo i ka wai. Ua kaka pū ʻo ia i ka laiki. Ma hope, ua kau lāua i nā pā ma luna o ka haka, a ua piha ka haka.

A laila, ua ʻohi ʻo Kaʻeloa i ka wahie kiawe ma kahakai o Waiʻanae. Ulu nui ke kiawe ma ka ʻaoʻao maloʻo o ka mokupuni, a he wahie maikaʻi ia no ka imu: ʻā lōʻihi ke kiawe, a wela loa. Ua ʻoki pū ʻo ia i kekahi ʻohe. Ua ʻoki ʻo ia ma lalo o kēlā me kēia pona, a ua lilo kēlā me kēia ʻāpana ʻohe i kīʻaha. Paʻa ka pona ma lalo, a ʻaʻole kahe ka wai i waho.

I ke kakahiaka o ka Pōʻaono, ua hoʻouka lāua i nā mea a pau i ke kaʻa: ka wahie kiawe, nā pahu ʻai, ʻelua ʻāhui maiʻa mai ko lāua māla, a me kekahi ʻeke ʻawa. Ua hoʻokele ʻo Kaʻeloa i ke kaʻa i Honolulu, a laila ma luna o nā pali i Kāneʻohe. Ua akahele ʻo ia ma nā hulina, i hāʻule ʻole nā ʻāhui maiʻa.

Ma Kāneʻohe, ua hana nā kāne i ka imu me ka wahie kiawe. Ua hoʻomākaukau nā kūpuna i ka ʻawa. Ua kuʻi lākou i ke aʻa ʻawa, ua hui pū lākou iā ia me ka wai, a ua inu lākou i ka ʻawa mai nā kīʻaha ʻohe a Kaʻeloa.

I ke ahiahi, ua hoʻākoakoa he haneli kānaka ma ka lūʻau. Ua ʻai lākou i ka puaʻa, ka lau kalo, ka iʻa me ka ʻakaʻakai, a me ka maiʻa. Ua ʻakaʻaka ka pēpē i ka ʻike ʻana i nā kānaka he nui.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka mea a Kaʻeloa i hoʻokala ai?
Ua hoʻokala ʻo ia i nā pahi.
No ke aha he wahie maikaʻi ke kiawe no ka imu?
No ka mea ʻā lōʻihi ke kiawe, a wela loa.
Ma hea i ʻoki ai ʻo Kaʻeloa i ka ʻohe?
Ua ʻoki ʻo ia ma lalo o kēlā me kēia pona.
He aha nā mea i hoʻouka ʻia i ke kaʻa?
Ka wahie kiawe, nā pahu ʻai, nā ʻāhui maiʻa, a me ka ʻawa.

lessons.title: Ka lāpaki ʻaeʻa
lessons.summary: Kaleilehua's lively rabbit escapes in Makawao and wanders across a grassy field into the next garden; she cuts across the field, shakes the bushes, builds a box trap and catches it, and her dog licks them both.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Kaleilehua ma Makawao, ma Maui, a he lāpaki keʻokeʻo kāna. ʻEleu loa ka lāpaki.

I kekahi kakahiaka, ua wehe ʻia ka puka o ka pahu lāpaki. Ua holo ka lāpaki i waho. Ua ʻaeʻa ʻo ia ma ka māla, a laila ma ke kula mauʻu ma kekahi ʻaoʻao o ke alanui. Ua hopohopo ʻo Kaleilehua.

Ua holo ʻo Kaleilehua ma kona paikikala ma ke alanui e ʻimi ana i ka lāpaki. Ua ʻike ʻo ia i ka lāpaki ma waena o ke kula mauʻu. Ua hele lala ʻo ia ma ke kula, mai kekahi kihi a i kekahi kihi, no ka mea ua pōkole ke ala lala. Ua haʻihaʻi nā lālā maloʻo ma lalo o kona mau wāwae. Ua lohe ka lāpaki i ka haʻihaʻi ʻana o nā lālā, a ua holo ʻeleu ʻo ia.

Ua komo ka lāpaki i loko o kekahi ulu lāʻau liʻiliʻi. Ua hoʻoluli ʻo Kaleilehua i nā lāʻau. Ua lele mai ka lāpaki i waho, ua peku ʻo ia me kona mau wāwae hope, a ua holo ʻo ia i ka māla o ka hale ma kekahi ʻaoʻao. Ma ia māla, ua ʻai malū ka lāpaki i nā lau ʻai a ka wahine o ia hale.

Ua hoʻoholo ʻo Kaleilehua e hana i kekahi pahele. Ua kau ʻo ia i kekahi pahu ma luna o kekahi lāʻau liʻiliʻi me ke kaula. Ma lalo o ka pahu, ua waiho ʻo ia i kekahi mau lau ʻai ʻono. Ke komo ka lāpaki ma lalo o ka pahu, e huki ana ʻo Kaleilehua i ke kaula, a e hāʻule ana ka pahu ma luna ona. Ua noho mū ʻo ia ma hope o kekahi kumulāʻau.

Ma hope o ka hapahā hola, ua hele malū mai ka lāpaki i ka pahele. Ua huki ʻo Kaleilehua i ke kaula, a ua hāʻule ka pahu. Ua paʻa ka lāpaki i loko o ka pahele! Ua peku ʻo ia, akā ʻaʻole hiki iā ia ke holo.

Ua lawe ʻo Kaleilehua i ka lāpaki i ka hale. Ma ka hale, ua palu kāna ʻīlio i ka maka o Kaleilehua, a ua palu pū ka ʻīlio i ka lāpaki. Ua pani pono ʻo Kaleilehua i ka puka o ka pahu, a ʻaʻole i ʻaeʻa hou ka lāpaki.

Nā nīnau:
Pehea ka lāpaki a Kaleilehua?
ʻEleu loa ka lāpaki.
Ua ʻaeʻa ka lāpaki i hea?
Ua ʻaeʻa ʻo ia ma ka māla a ma ke kula mauʻu.
No ke aha i hele lala ai ʻo Kaleilehua ma ke kula?
No ka mea ua pōkole ke ala lala.
He aha ka mea a ka lāpaki i ʻai malū ai?
Ua ʻai malū ʻo ia i nā lau ʻai a ka wahine.

lessons.title: Ke kolepa ma Lānaʻi
lessons.summary: Kauakahi, a retired chemistry teacher, takes his grandson Kahalau on the ferry from Lāhainā to Lānaʻi to play golf; they play kōnane on board, he teaches golf manners, explains the phosphorus that keeps the grass green, and they read an old photo caption over bread and honey.
lessons.text:
He kumu kemika ʻo Kauakahi ma mua, ma Wailuku. Ua hoʻomaha ʻo ia mai ka hana, a luana ʻo ia i kona mau lā. I kekahi Pōʻalua, ua hele ʻo ia me kāna moʻopuna, ʻo Kahalau, i Lānaʻi no ka pāʻani kolepa. Ua komo ʻo Kauakahi i kona lole kolepa lenalena. Ua hoʻoluʻu kāna wahine i kēlā lole me ka ʻōlena.

Ua eʻe lāua i ka moku ma Lāhainā. Ma ka moku, ua lawe mai ʻo Kauakahi i kekahi papa kōnane. He huinahā ka papa. He ʻeleʻele kekahi mau pōhaku, a he keakea nā pōhaku ʻē aʻe. Ua pāʻani lāua ma luna o ka papa huinahā. Ua lanakila ʻo Kauakahi i ka pāʻani mua, a ua lanakila ʻo Kahalau me nā pōhaku keakea i ka lua.

Ua ʻū ʻo Kauakahi. "Ua ʻeha koʻu kuamoʻo i ka noho ʻana ma kēia noho paʻakikī," wahi āna. Ua kū pololei ʻo ia, a ua ʻoluʻolu hou kona kuamoʻo. "E luana kāua i kēia lā," wahi āna.

Ma Lānaʻi, ua hiki lāua i ke kahua kolepa. ʻŌmaʻomaʻo loa ka mauʻu. Ua nīnau ʻo Kahalau, "No ke aha i ʻōmaʻomaʻo loa ai ka mauʻu? Maloʻo kēia mokupuni." Ua pane ke kumu kemika kahiko, "Hāʻawi nā limahana i ka wai a me kekahi mea hoʻoulu i ka mauʻu. Aia ka pokepola i loko o ia mea. He mea pono ka pokepola no nā mea kanu a pau, e like me ka ʻai no kākou."

Ma mua o ka pāʻani ʻana, ua aʻo ʻo Kauakahi i ka lawena o ke kolepa. "Mai walaʻau ke kuʻi kekahi i kāna kinipōpō. Mai holo ma ka mauʻu kokoke i ka puka. A inā hala kāu kinipōpō, mai ukiuki." Maikaʻi ka lawena o Kahalau. Ua hala kekahi mau kinipōpō āna, akā ʻaʻole ʻo ia i ukiuki.

Ma hope o ke kolepa, ua ʻai lāua ma kekahi hale ʻaina. Ua ʻai lāua i ka palaoa me ka meli. Ma ka paia, aia kekahi kiʻi kahiko o nā limahana ma ka mahi hala kahiki. Ua heluhelu ʻo Kahalau i ka lepe ma lalo o ke kiʻi: "Nā limahana hala kahiki, Lānaʻi, 1950." "Hiki paha iā Tūtū ke hoʻoluʻu i koʻu lole me ka ʻōlena?" wahi a Kahalau. Ua ʻakaʻaka ʻo Kauakahi, a ua ʻai hou lāua i ka meli.

Nā nīnau:
Na wai i hoʻoluʻu i ka lole kolepa o Kauakahi?
Na kāna wahine i hoʻoluʻu i ka lole.
He aha ke ʻano o ka papa kōnane?
He huinahā ka papa.
He aha ka mea i loko o ka mea hoʻoulu?
Aia ka pokepola i loko ona.
He aha ka mea ma ka lepe ma lalo o ke kiʻi?
"Nā limahana hala kahiki, Lānaʻi, 1950."
